$comment: The two denylists, refused where an SLO is actually written. Refused twice on purpose: `const` says node_memory_usage_bytes is not the metric the invoice SLI counts, and `not` says it is not a metric any SLI may count. One rule is a rule a well-meaning commit undoes — the whole reason metrics.schema.json names tenant_id in a `not` as well as omitting it from the allowlist. The errorSelector below is the same mistake wearing a hat: an infrastructure label in the bad-half matcher measures the machine instead of the behaviour, and it is the shape R6 rules out.

http_server_availability.description: Requests the service handled without a server error, over its whole surface.

authentication_succeeds.description: A caller can authenticate: a token request to the named route returns without a server error.

event_accepted_into_outbox.description: An event this service accepted is published, rather than sitting in the outbox waiting for someone to notice.

email_dispatched.description: An email the product asked for is handed to a provider without a refusal or a permanent failure.

invoice_computed.description: How much memory the billing service is using, which is not an SLO.
